title: A Finite-Volume Framework for Transient Mixed Flows in Urban Drainage Networks: Well-Balanced Second-Order Reconstruction and Closure Splitting Between the Preissmann Slot and the Two-Component Pressure Approach
content: Point-particle kinematics and projective measurement rely on two unbounded idealizations: exact spatial localization at finite energy and instantaneous collapse at infinite bandwidth. We formulate nonrelativistic quantum mechanics in canonical density--phase variables paired with a falsifiable information-capacity hypothesis. Axiom 1 takes an objective configuration density and compact phase field with finite Fisher information, quantized vortex circulation, and simple nodal phase matching as explicit kinematic inputs, ruling out point localization and addressing Wallstrom's objection. Axiom 2 pairs the Fisher localization energy with a Nyquist−Planck ceiling \(\Delta E_{\mathrm{int}}/\hbar\) on the operator-supremum port capacity, selected from the Bohr modulation bandwidth \(\Delta E_{\mathrm{int}}/h\) by the constitutive sampling threshold \(\mathcal{K} \le 1/4\). On regular charts, the density−phase manifold carries a weak Kähler structure isometric to the Fubini−Study metric; with form-domain and unitary-lift inputs, the closed limit recovers Schrödinger dynamics, bound-state spectra, and uncertainty relations. Under bounded continuous monitoring, the stochastic filter is globally well posed, yielding Born-weight selection under Postulate 1, linear Lindblad evolution for arbitrary detection efficiency, and local no-signaling. Coherent-pointer Holevo budgets and time-dependent circuit-QED sub-window diagnostics separate in-domain Markovian bounds from high-drive tests.
